{{Quote|We've got mongrel officers now, for fierfek's sake, and that one only got through the Academy because his dad's some ranking captain. If he could read a chart, he'd be dangerous. You should hear Pellaeon having a go at him. Pellaeon's all right, though. They're not all useless.|Clone trooper Tel|<ref name="TrueColors">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>}}
'''Republic officers''', known as '''mongrels''' in [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] [[List of phrases and slang/Legends|slang]], were the men and women commissioned into the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] and served in a command capacity.

==Description==
{{Quote|It's conduct unbecoming to an officer. They're supposed to be squeaky clean and upstanding.|Clone Captain Rex|<ref name="No Prisoners">''[[The Clone Wars: No Prisoners]]''</ref>}}
Republic [[Officer/Legends|officers]] served both onboard [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] and on the ground, directing both the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] and the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] under their command. The Republic officers were outranked by the members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]], the chief officers of the military such as [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]] and [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] were superseded in authority only by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].

==History==
The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] was not the only time the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] recruited men and women into its military. This practice has gone back as far as the [[Old Sith Wars]], when the Republic army fought against the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]] and [[Ulic Qel-Droma/Legends|Ulic Qel-Droma]] and during the subsequent [[Jedi Civil War]], when many, including [[Trask Ulgo|Ensign Trask Ulgo]] and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Forn Dodonna]], fought against the army of [[Darth Malak]], whose numbers included many of their former comrades, such as [[Saul Karath]], a [[Sith officer]].

During the Clone Wars, while [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] such as [[Clone Captain/Legends|Clone Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] displayed respect for their nonclone contemporaries,<ref name="No Prisoners" /> the term "[[Mongrel/Legends|mongrel]]" emerged within the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] ranks for those non-clones given commanding positions<ref name="TCSWE-Mongrel">{{CSWECite|II|327|mongrel}}</ref> and saw use by troopers such as [[Tel (clone trooper)|Tel]], who expressed a distain for most "mongrels." Even then, Tel made an exception for those who held skill, such as [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]].<ref name="TrueColors" /> Following the end of the Clone Wars, those Republic officers who were considered the brightest and most decorated of the conflict became [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Starfleet]] and [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. As part of the Imperial propaganda, many Imperial officers were falsely credited for many of the heroic acts that were performed by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] during the war.
